218: 		task := state.Tasks[idx]
219: 		mu.Unlock()
220: 		historyMu.Lock()
221: 		defer historyMu.Unlock()
222: 		return appendRunHistoryWithKeys(listing.Study, stateCopy, task, historyKeys)
223: 	}
224: 	for _, task := range state.Tasks {
225: 		if task.Status == TaskStatusRunning || task.Status == TaskStatusValidating || task.Status == TaskStatusRetrying {
226: 			emit(RunLoopProgressStarted, task)
227: 		}
228: 	}
229: 
230: 	var firstErr error
231: 	var errMu sync.Mutex
232: 	recordErr := func(err error) {
233: 		if err == nil {
234: 			return
235: 		}
236: 		errMu.Lock()
237: 		defer errMu.Unlock()
238: 		if firstErr == nil {
239: 			firstErr = err
240: 		}
241: 	}
242: 	loadFirstErr := func() error {
243: 		errMu.Lock()
244: 		defer errMu.Unlock()
245: 		return firstErr
246: 	}
247: 	var publicationJobs chan ExecutionResult
248: 	var publicationDone chan struct{}
249: 	if s.publisher != nil {

251: 		publicationDone = make(chan struct{})
252: 		go func() {
253: 			defer close(publicationDone)
254: 			for execution := range publicationJobs {
255: 				published, publishErr := s.publishExecution(ctx, execution)
256: 				if len(published.Publications) > 0 {

258: 				}
259: 				recordErr(publishErr)
260: 			}
261: 		}()
262: 	}
263: 	attempted := map[string]bool{}
264: 	runTask := func(id string) {

267: 			recordErr(recordHistory(id))
268: 			emitTask(RunLoopProgressCancelled, id)
269: 			return
270: 		}
271: 		task, err := taskSnapshot(id)
272: 		if err != nil {
273: 			recordErr(err)
274: 			return
275: 		}
276: 		mu.Lock()
277: 		dependencyState := cloneRunState(state)
278: 		mu.Unlock()
279: 		if !dependenciesComplete(dependencyState, task) {
280: 			if dependenciesTerminal(dependencyState, task) {
281: 				recordErr(markSynthesisDependenciesFailed(update, id))
282: 				recordErr(recordHistory(id))
283: 				emitTask(RunLoopProgressFailed, id)
284: 				return
285: 			}
286: 			recordErr(update(id, func(t *TaskState) {
287: 				t.Status = TaskStatusWaiting
288: 				t.UpdatedAt = time.Now().UTC()
289: 			}))
290: 			emitTask(RunLoopProgressWaiting, id)
291: 			return
292: 		}
293: 		recordErr(update(id, func(t *TaskState) {
294: 			now := time.Now().UTC()
295: 			t.Status = TaskStatusRunning
296: 			t.Attempts++
297: 			t.StartedAt = &now
298: 			t.CompletedAt = nil
299: 			t.UpdatedAt = now
300: 			t.LastError = nil
301: 			t.RetryAfter = nil
302: 			t.Agent = AgentMetadata{}
303: 		}))
304: 		diagnostics.sample("runtime.start", id, 0, nil)
305: 		runtimeStarted := time.Now()
306: 		var res ExecutionResult
307: 		checkpointSession := func(session TaskSession) {
308: 			recordErr(update(id, func(t *TaskState) {
309: 				copy := session
310: 				t.Session = &copy
311: 				t.UpdatedAt = time.Now().UTC()
312: 			}))
313: 		}
314: 		switch task.Kind {
315: 		case TaskKindAnalysis:
316: 			res, err = s.RunAnalysis(ctx, ExecutionRequest{StudyRef: listing.Study.Name, DimensionRef: task.DimensionRef, SourceRef: task.Source, Model: req.Model, ResumeSession: task.Session, DeferPublication: true, OnSession: checkpointSession, OnEvent: func(event runtimeEvent) {
317: 				emitRuntime(id, event)
318: 			}})
319: 			if err != nil {
320: 				res = ExecutionResult{Status: ExecutionStatusRuntimeFailed, TaskKind: TaskKindAnalysis, Study: listing.Study, OutputPath: task.OutputPath, RuntimeError: safeError(err), RuntimeErr: err}
321: 			}
322: 		case TaskKindSynthesis:
323: 			res, err = s.Synthesize(ctx, SynthesisRequest{StudyRef: listing.Study.Name, DimensionRef: task.DimensionRef, SourceRefs: selectedSourceNames(listing.Sources), Model: req.Model, ResumeSession: task.Session, DeferPublication: true, OnSession: checkpointSession, OnEvent: func(event runtimeEvent) {
324: 				emitRuntime(id, event)
325: 			}})
326: 			if err != nil {

328: 			}

332: 		}

335: 		recordErr(recordHistory(id))

338: 		}
339: 		emitTask(progressEventForExecution(res), id)
340: 	}
341: 	done := make(chan struct{}, req.Parallelism)
342: 	active := 0
343: 	stopScheduling := false
344: 	for active > 0 || (!stopScheduling && ctx.Err() == nil) {
345: 		if loadFirstErr() != nil {
346: 			stopScheduling = true
347: 		}
348: 		pressure := readMemoryPressure()
349: 		mu.Lock()
350: 		previousParallelism := effectiveParallelism
351: 		if pressure.Stretched && effectiveParallelism > 1 {
352: 			effectiveParallelism--
353: 		} else if pressure.Recovered && effectiveParallelism < req.Parallelism {
354: 			effectiveParallelism++
355: 		}
356: 		memoryAvailable = pressure.AvailableBytes
357: 		if effectiveParallelism != previousParallelism {
358: 			if effectiveParallelism < previousParallelism {
359: 				schedulingMessage = fmt.Sprintf("memory pressure reduced parallelism from %d to %d", previousParallelism, effectiveParallelism)
360: 				diagnostics.scheduling("parallelism.throttled", req.Parallelism, effectiveParallelism, pressure.AvailableBytes)
361: 			} else {
362: 				schedulingMessage = fmt.Sprintf("memory recovered; restored parallelism from %d to %d", previousParallelism, effectiveParallelism)
363: 				diagnostics.scheduling("parallelism.restored", req.Parallelism, effectiveParallelism, pressure.AvailableBytes)
364: 			}
365: 		}
366: 		parallelismChanged := effectiveParallelism != previousParallelism
367: 		changeEvent := RunLoopProgressRestored
368: 		if effectiveParallelism < previousParallelism {
369: 			changeEvent = RunLoopProgressThrottled
370: 		}
371: 		mu.Unlock()
372: 		if parallelismChanged {
373: 			emit(changeEvent, TaskState{})
374: 		}
375: 		disk := readSchedulerDiskPressure(listing.Study.Path)
376: 		if disk.Pressured {
377: 			// When no worker can make progress, retained stores must not pin the
378: 			// scheduler below its admission threshold forever. Active workers keep
379: 			// their resumable stores unless pressure becomes critical.
380: 			aggressiveCleanup := disk.Critical || active == 0
381: 			cleanup := runtimepkg.CleanupRuntimeStores(listing.Study.Path, 72*time.Hour, 2*1024*1024*1024, aggressiveCleanup)
382: 			diagnostics.storage("disk.admission_paused", cleanup, disk)
383: 			disk = readSchedulerDiskPressure(listing.Study.Path)
384: 			if disk.Pressured {
385: 				mu.Lock()
386: 				schedulingMessage = fmt.Sprintf("disk pressure paused new workers; %.1f%% used, %d MiB available", disk.UsedPercent, disk.AvailableBytes/(1024*1024))
387: 				mu.Unlock()
388: 				if active > 0 {
389: 					<-done
390: 					active--
391: 					continue
392: 				}
393: 				timer := time.NewTimer(30 * time.Second)
394: 				select {
395: 				case <-ctx.Done():
396: 					timer.Stop()
397: 				case <-timer.C:
398: 				}
399: 				continue
400: 			}
401: 		}
402: 		diskCap := diskParallelismCap(disk, req.Parallelism)
403: 		if diskCap > 0 && diskCap < effectiveParallelism {
404: 			mu.Lock()
405: 			previous := effectiveParallelism
406: 			effectiveParallelism = diskCap
407: 			schedulingMessage = fmt.Sprintf("disk headroom reduced parallelism from %d to %d", previous, effectiveParallelism)
408: 			mu.Unlock()
409: 			diagnostics.scheduling("parallelism.disk_throttled", req.Parallelism, effectiveParallelism, disk.AvailableBytes)
410: 			emit(RunLoopProgressThrottled, TaskState{})
411: 		}
412: 		available := effectiveParallelism - active
413: 		var ids []string
414: 		var nextRetry *time.Time
415: 		mu.Lock()
416: 		now := time.Now().UTC()
417: 		if !stopScheduling && available > 0 {
418: 			ids = runnableTaskIDs(state, scope, attempted, available, now, listing.DimensionOrder)
419: 			nextRetry = nextRetryAfter(state, scope, now)
420: 		}
421: 		mu.Unlock()
422: 		for _, id := range ids {
423: 			attempted[id] = true
424: 			active++
425: 			// Emit Started at claim time so progress ordering matches the
426: 			// scheduler's deterministic tier order rather than racing worker
427: 			// goroutines.
428: 			emitTask(RunLoopProgressStarted, id)
429: 			go func(id string) {
430: 				runTask(id)
431: 				done <- struct{}{}
432: 			}(id)
433: 		}
434: 		if active > 0 {
435: 			// Each task owns its OpenCode database, so a completed slot can be
436: 			// refilled without waiting for sibling cleanup.
437: 			<-done
438: 			active--
439: 			continue
440: 		}
441: 		if stopScheduling || (len(ids) == 0 && nextRetry == nil) {
442: 			break
443: 		}
444: 		waitUntilRetry(ctx, *nextRetry, func() {
445: 			mu.Lock()
446: 			defer mu.Unlock()
447: 			emitRetryWait(state, scope, result.StatePath, req.Progress)
448: 		})
449: 	}
450: 	if publicationJobs != nil {
451: 		close(publicationJobs)
452: 		<-publicationDone
453: 	}
454: 	if err := loadFirstErr(); err != nil {
455: 		return result, err
456: 	}
457: 
458: 	state.Complete = allTasksComplete(state)
459: 	if err := save(); err != nil {
460: 		return result, err
461: 	}
462: 	if err := SyncRunHistory(listing.Study, state); err != nil {
463: 		return result, err
464: 	}
465: 	if s.publisher != nil {
466: 		publication, publishErr := s.publishRunLoopState(ctx, listing.Study)
467: 		if len(publication) > 0 {
468: 			result.Publications = append(result.Publications, publication...)
469: 		}
470: 		if publishErr != nil {
471: 			return result, publishErr
472: 		}
473: 	}
474: 	result.State = state
475: 	result.Counts = runLoopCounts(state)
476: 	result.ScopeCounts = runLoopCounts(filterRunState(state, scope))
477: 	result.Status = runLoopStatus(filterRunState(state, scope), result.ScopeCounts, ctx.Err() != nil)
478: 	return result, nil
479: }

481: func waitUntilRetry(ctx context.Context, retryAt time.Time, emit func()) {
482: 	for {
483: 		if emit != nil {
484: 			emit()
485: 		}
486: 		wait := time.Until(retryAt)
487: 		if wait <= 0 {
488: 			return
489: 		}
490: 		if wait > time.Minute {
491: 			wait = time.Minute
492: 		}
493: 		timer := time.NewTimer(wait)
494: 		select {
495: 		case <-ctx.Done():
496: 			timer.Stop()
497: 			return
498: 		case <-timer.C:
499: 		}
500: 	}
501: }

503: func emitRetryWait(state RunState, scope map[string]bool, statePath string, progress func(RunLoopProgress)) {
504: 	if progress == nil {
505: 		return
506: 	}
507: 	for _, task := range state.Tasks {
508: 		if !scope[task.ID] {
509: 			continue
510: 		}
511: 		if task.Status == TaskStatusRetrying && task.RetryAfter != nil && task.RetryAfter.After(time.Now().UTC()) {
512: 			progress(RunLoopProgress{Event: RunLoopProgressWaiting, Task: task, Counts: SummarizeRunStateCounts(state, statePath), ScopeCounts: summarizeRunStateCountsForScope(state, scope, statePath)})
513: 			return
514: 		}
515: 	}
516: }

518: func summarizeRunStateCountsForScope(state RunState, scope map[string]bool, statePath string) StatusSummary {
519: 	if len(scope) == 0 {
520: 		return StatusSummary{Complete: true, StatePath: statePath, RunID: state.RunID}
521: 	}
522: 	summary := StatusSummary{Complete: true, StatePath: statePath, RunID: state.RunID}
523: 	for _, task := range state.Tasks {
524: 		if !scope[task.ID] {
525: 			continue
526: 		}
527: 		summary.Total++
528: 		countTaskStatus(&summary, task)
529: 		if task.Status != TaskStatusCompleted && task.Status != TaskStatusSkipped {
530: 			summary.Complete = false
531: 		}
532: 	}
533: 	return summary
534: }

575: func progressEventForExecution(res ExecutionResult) RunLoopProgressEvent {
576: 	switch res.Status {
577: 	case ExecutionStatusCompleted, ExecutionStatusSkipped:
578: 		return RunLoopProgressCompleted
579: 	case ExecutionStatusCancelled:

600: func runnableTaskIDs(state RunState, scope map[string]bool, attempted map[string]bool, limit int, now time.Time, dimensionOrder []Dimension) []string {
601: 	if limit < 1 {
602: 		limit = 1
603: 	}
604: 	var ids []string
605: 	byID := map[string]TaskState{}
606: 	for _, task := range state.Tasks {
607: 		byID[task.ID] = task
608: 	}
609: 	ranks := dimensionPriorityRanks(dimensionOrder)
610: 	remainingRank := len(dimensionOrder)
611: 	// Dimension order remains a priority, but not a barrier: lower-priority
612: 	// dimensions backfill any workers the earlier tiers cannot occupy.
613: 	for rank := 0; rank <= remainingRank; rank++ {
614: 		for _, kind := range []TaskKind{TaskKindSynthesis, TaskKindAnalysis} {
615: 			for _, task := range state.Tasks {
616: 				if len(ids) >= limit {
617: 					return ids
618: 				}
619: 				if !scope[task.ID] || taskAttemptBlocked(task, attempted) || task.Kind != kind || !taskRunnable(task, now) {
620: 					continue
621: 				}
622: 				if dimensionTaskRank(task, ranks, remainingRank) != rank {
623: 					continue
624: 				}
625: 				if kind == TaskKindSynthesis && !dependenciesCompleteFrom(byID, task) && !dependenciesTerminalFrom(byID, task) {
626: 					continue
627: 				}
628: 				ids = append(ids, task.ID)
629: 			}
630: 		}
631: 	}
632: 	return ids
633: }

635: func dimensionPriorityRanks(order []Dimension) map[string]int {
636: 	ranks := make(map[string]int, len(order))
637: 	for i, dimension := range order {
638: 		ranks[dimension.Ref()] = i
639: 	}
640: 	return ranks
641: }

643: func dimensionTaskRank(task TaskState, ranks map[string]int, remainingRank int) int {
644: 	if rank, ok := ranks[task.DimensionRef]; ok {
645: 		return rank
646: 	}
647: 	return remainingRank
648: }

650: func runLoopScope(study Study, allSources []Source, scopeSources []Source, dimensions []Dimension, sourceFiltered bool) map[string]bool {

653: 		applicable := GetApplicableSources(scopeSources, dimension)
654: 		if len(applicable) == 0 {

656: 		}

668: func filterRunState(state RunState, scope map[string]bool) RunState {
669: 	if len(scope) == 0 {
670: 		out := state
671: 		out.Tasks = nil
672: 		out.Complete = true
673: 		return out
674: 	}
675: 	out := state
676: 	out.Tasks = make([]TaskState, 0, len(state.Tasks))
677: 	for _, task := range state.Tasks {
678: 		if scope[task.ID] {
679: 			out.Tasks = append(out.Tasks, task)
680: 		}
681: 	}
682: 	out.Complete = allTasksComplete(out)

686: func taskAttemptBlocked(task TaskState, attempted map[string]bool) bool {
687: 	return attempted[task.ID] && task.Status != TaskStatusRetrying

690: func taskRunnable(task TaskState, now time.Time) bool {
691: 	switch task.Status {
692: 	case TaskStatusPending, TaskStatusFailed, TaskStatusCancelled, TaskStatusWaiting:
693: 		if task.RetryAfter != nil && task.RetryAfter.After(now) {
694: 			return false
695: 		}
696: 		return true
697: 	case TaskStatusRetrying:
698: 		return task.RetryAfter == nil || !task.RetryAfter.After(now)
699: 	default:
700: 		return false
701: 	}
702: }

704: func nextRetryAfter(state RunState, scope map[string]bool, now time.Time) *time.Time {
705: 	var next *time.Time
706: 	for _, task := range state.Tasks {
707: 		if !scope[task.ID] {
708: 			continue
709: 		}
710: 		if task.Status != TaskStatusRetrying || task.RetryAfter == nil || !task.RetryAfter.After(now) {
711: 			continue
712: 		}
713: 		retry := *task.RetryAfter
714: 		if next == nil || retry.Before(*next) {
715: 			next = &retry
716: 		}
717: 	}
718: 	return next
719: }

721: func dependenciesComplete(state RunState, task TaskState) bool {

725: 	}

731: 		if byID[dep.TaskID].Status != TaskStatusCompleted {
732: 			return false
733: 		}
734: 	}

740: 	for _, task := range state.Tasks {
741: 		byID[task.ID] = task
742: 	}
743: 	var ids []string
744: 	for _, task := range state.Tasks {

747: 		}

30: 	}

297: 		case TaskStatusRetrying:

302: 			}

310: 				}
311: 				task.UpdatedAt = now
312: 			}
313: 		case TaskStatusCompleted:

315: 			switch task.Kind {
316: 			case TaskKindAnalysis:

326: 					continue
327: 				}
328: 				result = ValidateSourceReport(study, source, dimension)
329: 			case TaskKindSynthesis:
330: 				dimension, dimensionOK := dimensionByRef[task.DimensionRef]
331: 				if !dimensionOK {
332: 					dimension, dimensionOK = dimensionByRef[task.Dimension]
333: 				}
334: 				if !dimensionOK {

336: 					task.LastError = &TaskError{Code: "validation.reference", Message: "completed task references unknown dimension"}
337: 					task.UpdatedAt = now
338: 					continue
339: 				}
340: 				result = ValidateFinalReport(study, dimension)

342: 				continue
343: 			}
344: 			summary := validationSummary(result, now)
345: 			task.Validation = &summary

380: 		dimensionByRef[dimension.Number] = dimension
381: 	}
382: 	restoreKind := func(kind TaskKind) {
383: 		for i := range state.Tasks {
384: 			task := &state.Tasks[i]
385: 			record, ok := completed[task.ID]

399: 			}

401: 				source, sourceOK := sourceByKey[sourceKey(task.Source, task.SourceKind)]
402: 				if !sourceOK {
403: 					continue
404: 				}
405: 				validation = ValidateSourceReport(study, source, dimension)
406: 			} else {
407: 				validation = ValidateFinalReport(study, dimension)
408: 			}
409: 			if validation.Status != ValidationStatusPassed {
410: 				continue
411: 			}
412: 			task.Status = TaskStatusCompleted
413: 			summary := validationSummary(validation, now)
414: 			task.Validation = &summary
415: 			task.LastError = nil
416: 			task.RetryAfter = nil
417: 			task.UpdatedAt = now
418: 			if record.CompletedAt != nil {
419: 				completedAt := *record.CompletedAt
420: 				task.CompletedAt = &completedAt
421: 			} else {
422: 				completedAt := now
423: 				task.CompletedAt = &completedAt
424: 			}
425: 		}

1. `ReconcileRunState`: when prior exists, it takes `current[i] = prior` then refreshes projections. But it does NOT preserve `CreatedAt`? It does — prior carries CreatedAt. It refreshes Dimension/DimensionRef/Source/SourceKind/OutputPath/Dependencies. Note: if a task's dimension Number changed (dimension renumbered), the task ID changes (ID includes dimension.Number) → prior not found → new pending task created; old task dropped. Old task state lost silently (history retains evidence). OK.

2. `ResumeValidateRunState` for completed tasks: validates and on failure sets Status=Failed with LastError "validation.report". BUT: it doesn't clear `CompletedAt`. So a Failed task with CompletedAt set from the prior completion... Then RestoreCompletedRunHistory only restores Pending tasks, so this Failed stays failed → scheduler reruns it (taskRunnable allows Failed without future RetryAfter; attempted map fresh). Rerun claims: clears CompletedAt at claim (`t.CompletedAt = nil`). Fine-ish.

Wait, actually there's something subtle in ResumeValidateRunState: for completed analysis tasks where source/dimension lookup fails → `validation.reference` failure. When can that happen? Reconcile rebuilt graph from current sources/dimensions; a completed prior task whose ID is still in current graph means source+kind still exist. So reference failure requires ID match but sourceKey mismatch? ID includes slug of name + kind. Hmm, sourceKey uses raw name+kind; slugID normalizes. Two different names could slug to same ID ("My Source" vs "my-source")! Then prior task with source "My Source" matches new graph ID built from "my-source"... wait no, reconcile maps by ID; current[i] gets prior's state but refreshed Source = current source name. Resume-validate looks up sourceByKey[task.Source, task.SourceKind] — refreshed, so found. OK consistent.

3. `RestoreCompletedRunHistory`: restores analysis first, then synthesis — with dependenciesComplete check for synthesis evaluated against *state* which now includes restored analyses. Good ordering.

But note: restore uses record.CompletedAt but NOT record.Attempts — attempts counter resets? No wait, restore only touches status/validation/completedat; task.Attempts stays whatever reconcile left (prior state preserved). OK.

7. `syncDir` ignores errors — noted in pack unknown #6.

reasoning_details.text:
Observations on locks.go:

1. **`AcquireRunLoopLock` stale-lock race**: after removing a dead-PID lock, it retries O_EXCL once; if EEXIST again, it errors with the *new* owner. Reasonable.

2. **Lock file written AFTER creation**: `os.OpenFile(O_EXCL)` creates empty file, then write content. A concurrent `ReadRunLoopLock` (e.g., `study status`) between create and write reads an EMPTY file → json.Unmarshal fails → "parse lock ... " error surfaces in status. Minor observability glitch, transient. Also: if the process crashes between O_EXCL create and content write, the lock file is empty forever → next acquire gets EEXIST → ReadRunLoopLock fails → "exists and could not be read" → ErrStudyLocked, requiring --force-unlock. That's a fail-closed crash window: crash in a ~microsecond window bricks resume until force-unlock. Hmm — but wait, actually the stale-cleanup path only triggers when the lock can be read AND PID dead. An empty/corrupt lock file cannot be auto-recovered. Is this worth reporting? The window is tiny but the outcome requires manual intervention. Also `CancelRunLoop` would fail with parse error. It's a known trade-off of O_EXCL pidfiles. Severity low, confidence medium. Actually more interesting: **write failure removes the lock** (`_ = os.Remove(path)`) — good.

3. **`Release()` ownership check compares `AcquiredAt.Equal`** — AcquiredAt serialized as RFC3339 with nanoseconds? time.Time JSON marshal keeps nanoseconds. Equal works after unmarshal. But note: lock file could be re-written by another acquirer with same PID? Same PID + same study + identical timestamp — impossible practically.

Wait, there IS a subtle issue in Release: it returns nil when lock doesn't exist (ErrNotExist). If another process used --force-unlock while we're running, our Release silently succeeds. Fine.

4. **`CancelRunLoop` checks `info.Study != "" && info.Study != study.Name`** — a lock file with empty Study field bypasses the name check (defensive against old format?). Then signals whatever PID. Attacker-controlled? The lock file lives in workspace tree at 0644; anyone with write access to the workspace can put PID X and empty study name... but if you have workspace write access you can do worse. Not a real boundary crossing. Skip.

5. `processAlive`: EPERM counted alive — correct for foreign-user PIDs. PID reuse noted in pack unknowns (#2): kill(pid,0) succeeding for recycled PID makes stale lock look live → user must force-unlock. Known limitation, documented direction in Sprint 35 FUTURE-INTENT. reasoning_details.text:
run_history.go observations:

**H11 (history read semantics): `readRunHistory` "pending" logic.** It treats a non-`pending` line as the current record; on the NEXT scan, it decodes `pending`. So malformed record at position k fails when reading line k+1... Actually: for each scanned line, first decode previous pending, then set pending=line. At EOF, decode final pending, ignoring error. So a malformed NON-final record causes hard failure at next iteration — good. A malformed FINAL record is silently ignored — matches "trailing partial line tolerated". BUT what about an empty line mid-file? `if len(line)==0 { pending = nil; continue }` — wait, that DISCARDS the pending record without decoding it! Let me re-trace:

```
for scanner.Scan() {
    line := copy of scanner.Bytes()
    if len(pending) > 0 {
        record, err := decodeRunHistoryRecord(pending)
        if err != nil { return nil, err }
        records = append(records, record)
    }
    if len(line) == 0 {
        pending = nil
        continue
    }
    pending = line
}
```

Sequence: line1="A" → pending empty → pending="A". line2="" (empty) → pending="A" nonempty → decode "A" append; then len(line)==0 → pending=nil. OK! The decode happens BEFORE the empty check. So empty lines flush the pending record. Good, no loss.

What about blank-line-separated? Fine.

BUT: `appendRunHistoryWithKeys` writes whole file via read+trim+rewrite per append — O(file) I/O per terminal transition, with fsync. For N tasks → O(N²) bytes written + N fsyncs of growing file. Performance hazard on large studies: e.g., each record ~1KB; 1000 tasks → sum ~ 500MB written through temp+fsync. Combined with cloneRunState per record. Real but scaling-dependent. Note as performance hazard candidate (C-perf). Tests won't catch.

**H12: dedup key includes CompletedAt RFC3339Nano.** Two terminal transitions with identical runID|taskID|attempts|completedAt collapse. When could two DIFFERENT meaningful outcomes share all four? Task failed at attempt 2 at time T (recorded), then... within same invocation attempted blocks rerun. Across invocations, ResumeValidate may promote Failed→Pending (only if RetryAfter present) or leave Failed (rerun on new invocation!). Rerun: claim clears CompletedAt, sets StartedAt=now, Attempts++ → new key differs by attempts. Same attempts count can't recur because claim always increments. EXCEPT markTaskCancelled/markSynthesisDependenciesFailed paths which don't increment attempts... those don't produce duplicate keys either since time differs (nanosecond clock granularity — could two updates in same nanosecond? No).

Hmm wait, actually there IS one: RestoreCompletedRunHistory restores CompletedAt from history record; then SyncRunHistory appends a record with that SAME completedAt and SAME attempts (task.Attempts preserved from prior state)... but the key already exists in historyKeys cache → skipped. Good, that's exactly why keys are preloaded.

**H13: `SyncRunHistory` calls WriteRunHistorySummary unconditionally** — even when nothing changed. Rewrites summary.md every RunLoop startup/epilogue. Minor.

**H14: trimInvalidTrailingRunHistory only trims ONE trailing invalid record** ("at most one"). If crash left TWO partial lines? Appends happen via atomic rename, so partial file content can only come from... atomicWriteRunHistory uses temp+rename — the target is never partially written! So how does a trailing partial line ever occur? Only from external corruption. Hmm wait — tasks.jsonl is ONLY written via atomicWriteRunHistory (temp+fsync+rename). Then a trailing partial line is impossible from this code path. The trim logic defends against externally-corrupted files. And readRunHistory tolerates malformed FINAL record silently. Consistent-ish. But note asymmetry: LoadRunHistory (used for restore) silently DROPS malformed final record while appendRunHistoryWithKeys REWRITES file trimming it. OK.

Wait, actually there's something interesting: **atomicWriteRunHistory does NOT syncDir after rename** unlike state.go. Directory entry durability not guaranteed. Minor durability asymmetry. Crash after rename before dir sync could lose the ledger file revert to older version — acceptable-ish, ledger is derived evidence.

memory_pressure.go:

**H15: hysteresis gap:** stretch < 15% (min 1GiB); recover > 25% (min 1.5GiB). Between 15–25%: neither Stretched nor Recovered → parallelism unchanged. Below stretch threshold: Stretched=true, Recovered=false. Above recovery: Recovered=true, Stretched=false?? Wait: `Stretched: available < stretchThreshold, Recovered: available > recoveryThreshold`. If available > recovery > stretch → Stretched false, Recovered true. Good hysteresis. But note both can be FALSE in the band — fine. Both never true simultaneously. OK.

Edge: total*15/100 with uint64 overflow? No.

If MemAvailable == 0 exactly (OOM extreme): returns memoryPressure{} (no pressure signals!) because `available == 0` check. Ha — under TRUE memory exhaustion where MemAvailable reads 0, the throttle reports NO pressure. But realistically MemAvailable never hits exact 0. Also parse failure → no pressure → scheduler proceeds full blast. Silent degradation noted in pack (#7). On non-Linux: /proc missing → zero values → no throttling. Platform assumption documented? "Platform assumption: Linux" per pack. Not report-worthy alone.

disk_pressure.go:

**H16: diskParallelismCap returns requested when TotalBytes==0 (statfs error)** — fail-open on statfs error. Admission pause also keyed off Pressured=false on statfs failure. Fail-open design consistent with memory. Documented anywhere? It's a deliberate choice presumably. Under statfs failure (e.g., network FS hiccup), scheduler runs unthrottled onto a possibly-full disk. Runtime children would fail writes anyway. Low.

Now diagnostics and remaining files.

330: 	}
331: 	text := string(data)

333: 	if end < 0 {
334: 		return 0, 0
335: 	}
336: 	fields := strings.Fields(text[end+1:])
337: 	if len(fields) < 20 {

341: 	systemTicks, errSystem := strconv.ParseUint(fields[12], 10, 64)
342: 	startTicks, errStart := strconv.ParseUint(fields[19], 10, 64)
343: 	if errUser != nil || errSystem != nil || errStart != nil {

Diagnostics observations:

**H17 (diagnostics deadlock candidate):** `d.sample()` acquires `d.mu`, and inside the locked section calls `childProcessResources(activeTasks)` → reads /proc files — fine. `d.append` also locks `d.mu`... wait: `sample()` does `d.mu.Lock()` ... `d.mu.Unlock()` then calls `d.append(sample)` which locks again. Not nested. OK.

BUT: `sample()` is called from `start()` goroutine every 5s AND from scheduler/worker paths (`diagnostics.sample("runtime.start"...)` in runTask, "state.save.end" inside persist under saveMu!). persist holds saveMu while calling diagnostics.sample which does file I/O + ReadMemStats (stop-the-world) + /proc reads. That's slow but not deadlock.

**H18: `childProcessResources` reads `/proc/self/task/<pid>/children` where pid = os.Getpid()** — /proc/self/task/$$/children lists children of the main thread? Actually /proc/<tgid>/task/<tgid>/children lists children of that thread's... it lists child tasks of the given task ID. Using the TGID gives all children of the process. Fine.

**H19: SummarizeParallelismThrottle iterates samples; `summary.LastAt = sample.Timestamp` on each throttled event — ends with last event. Requested/Effective take last nonzero. Decreased compares. OK.

**H20 (real candidate): diagnostics `append` rotation removes `.1` unconditionally even if a reader is mid-read** (LoadRunLoopResourceHistory opens .1 then current; rotation renames current→.1 replacing the file the reader may have open — on Linux open FD survives; fine).

**H21: LoadRunLoopResourceHistory limit semantics**: silently maps out-of-range limits to 240. Meh.

state_database.go:

**H22: loadRunStateDatabase unmarshals header into RunState then appends items WITHOUT ordering by Ordinal!** `for _, item := range record.Items { state.Tasks = append(...) }`. Context pack says "one item per task keyed by task.ID, ordinal order". Does store.Load return items ordered by Ordinal? Need to check productstate.Load implementation. If items come back ordered by key or insertion order rather than Ordinal, state.Tasks order differs from file-based order. Does order matter? runLoopCounts etc. don't depend on order; runnableTaskIDs iterates state.Tasks for candidates but rank-sorts by dimension; deterministic-ish. ValidateRunState doesn't require order. History restore doesn't care. Probably benign, but let me verify productstate ordering anyway.

**H23: DB-authoritative mode + `archiveRunStateIfExists` on --reset:** reset archives the FILE, but if state is DB-authoritative, the DB row still exists! loadOrCreateRunLoopState: req.Reset → archiveRunStateIfExists(study) renames file (may not exist since DB-authoritative skips file writes when !Complete) → NewRunState builds fresh state with new RunID → SaveRunState → RunStateInDatabase(study) still TRUE (old row!) → saveRunStateDatabase OVERWRITES the row with new state. But WAIT — bigger issue: **reset with DB authority: archiveRunStateIfExists archives a STALE file checkpoint (from completion time), while the authoritative recent state lived in the DB and is now overwritten without archiving.** Data loss of the prior run's final state? reasoning_details.text:
Interesting: `retryAfterFromAgent` takes MIN over policy decisions and attempts. Note in `applyExecutionResult`:

```go
if retryAfter := retryAfterFromAgent(t.Agent); retryAfter != nil {
    t.RetryAfter = retryAfter
}
```

Then for the default (runtime-failed) branch:
```go
if executionShouldRetry(res) {
    t.Status = TaskStatusRetrying
    if t.RetryAfter == nil { ...default... }
}
```

So agent-derived retryAfter is set even when status becomes Completed/Failed! E.g., res.Status == ExecutionStatusCompleted but Agent has retry decisions → RetryAfter set on a COMPLETED task. Then... completed branch sets `t.RetryAfter = nil`. OK good. Cancelled branch: doesn't clear RetryAfter — cancelled with stale future RetryAfter. Then taskRunnable(Cancelled) blocked until RetryAfter passes; ResumeValidate clears RetryAfter for cancelled→pending at next startup. Within same invocation, cancelled task not rerun anyway (ctx dead). Minor.

ValidationFailed/PreflightBlocked branch: sets Failed, doesn't touch RetryAfter. If agent metadata carried retryAfter (from a policy decision during the run), a FAILED validation task now has a FUTURE RetryAfter. Within this invocation: attempted blocks re-claim. Across invocations: ResumeValidate promotes Failed+future-RetryAfter → RETRYING (run_state.go:303-312). Hmm — so validation_failed tasks whose runtime emitted retry hints become retrying after restart. Is that wrong? The retry taxonomy says only rate_limit/timeout/provider_unavailable/runtime_unavailable are retryable. But applyExecutionResult's RetryAfter assignment happens BEFORE the switch, unconditionally from agent metadata. So a validation.failed result that includes agent attempts with RetryAfter (e.g., an earlier attempt hit rate limit, then final attempt produced invalid output) gets RetryAfter persisted. On resume it's promoted to Retrying and re-run. That contradicts "validation failures don't retry"... but arguably user wants rerun on next invocation anyway. Actually wait — even without RetryAfter, Failed tasks ARE runnable across invocations (attempted map is per-invocation). So any failed analysis re-runs on every `study run-loop` invocation regardless. That makes RetryAfter semantics mostly cosmetic across invocations. Not a strong defect.

Now the more serious verification-lens candidates I should chase:

**Candidate A: `waitUntilRetry` busy-wait emits progress every ≤60s; fine.**

**Candidate B: main loop `<-done` while disk-pressured with active>0: no ctx select — if all workers hang (runtime ignores ctx?), loop stuck until worker exits. Runtime boundary cancels via ctx though. OK.

**Candidate C: THE BIG ONE — check `emitTask(RunLoopProgressStarted, id)` + `active++` before goroutine spawn; if `ids` non-empty but `stopScheduling` flips mid-spawn... ids computed under !stopScheduling. Fine.

**Candidate D: `persist()` coalescing race**: two concurrent persists: P1 (task A) grabs saveMu, waits 250ms timer, clones state v5, saves, persistedVersion=5. P2 (task B) entered saveMu after P1 released; requestedVersion=6 (>persisted 5); waits maybe 250ms since lastPersisted just updated → sleeps ~250ms; clones v6; saves. OK — eventual persistence guaranteed because each update() calls persist which always eventually saves if version newer. BUT what if persist returns ctx.Err() during its debounce wait? update() returns that error → recordErr marks firstErr → stopScheduling. During cancellation that's expected-ish. But consider: ctx cancelled while workers still draining — persist aborts with context.DeadlineExceeded BEFORE saving, so terminal transitions from drain phase may never be persisted! Look at runTask cancel path: markTaskCancelled(update...) — update→persist→ctx.Done() during debounce wait → returns error → state not saved. Then RunLoop exits loop (ctx.Err()!=nil), skips firstErr path? No wait — recordErr(markTaskCancelled(...)) SET firstErr = context.Canceled! Then epilogue: `if err := loadFirstErr(); err != nil { return result, err }` — **cancellation via SIGINT produces firstErr=context.Canceled → early return → SKIPS the final forced save AND SyncRunHistory AND publish!**

Hold on. This is significant. Let me trace precisely:

1. User hits Ctrl-C → ctx cancelled.
2. Workers' runtime calls return cancelled results → applyExecutionResult → update() → persist(id,false): waits on timer/select; ctx.Done() fires → returns ctx.Err() (= context.Canceled). So applyExecutionResult returns error → recordErr(context.Canceled). The TASK STATE UPDATE was applied in-memory (update applies fn then persists; fn mutation already done under mu) but NOT SAVED to disk.
3. Also markTaskCancelled path similar.
4. Loop drains; publicationJobs closed & drained.
5. `loadFirstErr()` non-nil (context.Canceled recorded) → **return result, err — WITHOUT the final `save()`**.
6. Deferred lock.Release runs; lock file removed.
7. Result status never computed; CLI maps error.

So on Ctrl-C: the durable contract ("cancellation stops scheduling, cancels active runtime runs, waits, saves, records cancelled/retryable tasks" — Sprint AC :50) is violated whenever ANY persist hits the cancelled debounce window OR recordErr captured anything. Wait — actually does firstErr get set by context.Canceled in other paths too? `recordErr(publishErr)` in publisher goroutine: publishExecution(ctx...) with cancelled ctx → gitpublish errors with context canceled → firstErr set. And runTask's `res` from RunAnalysis with cancelled ctx: RunAnalysis returns result with Status cancelled (not error) usually; but startRuntime may return err (context.Canceled) → res.RuntimeFailed → applyExecutionResult → update → persist fails w/ ctx err → recordErr.

Hmm wait, actually let me double-check: does `update` fail when ctx cancelled? persist():
```go
if !force {
    if wait := 250ms - time.Since(lastPersisted); wait > 0 {
        select { case <-ctx.Done(): return ctx.Err(); case <-timer.C: }
    }
}
```
Only if within 250ms of last persist. If ≥250ms elapsed since lastPersisted, no wait → proceeds to clone & SaveRunState (which itself doesn't take ctx — file write proceeds). So whether the drain-phase persists succeed depends on timing relative to lastPersisted. Racy: sometimes saved, sometimes not.

But EVEN IF all drain-phase persists succeed, firstErr may still be set from OTHER recordErr calls with ctx-cancelled errors: e.g., publishExecution in the publisher goroutine uses ctx → returns error once ctx cancelled → recordErr. Or RunAnalysis internal ListStudy etc. don't use ctx. Or `recordErr(err)` from runTask's `err` variable — RunAnalysis returns (result, nil) mostly...

Actually wait, there's a cleaner question: is there ANY test pinning "SIGINT cancel → final save happens"? Context pack says AC:50 "cancellation stops scheduling, cancels active runtime runs, waits, saves, records cancelled/retryable tasks, exits with cancellation convention". Let me look at the tests to see how cancellation is verified. run_loop_test.go scenarios.

Also note the deferred release: `if releaseErr := lock.Release(); err == nil && releaseErr != nil { err = releaseErr }` — named return err. On the early-return path `return result, err` where err=firstErr — fine.

Now the CLI side: mapStudyRunLoopError(context.Canceled)? Let me check app/study_commands.go:354 area later. If exit code treats it as failure rather than cancellation convention, that compounds.

Let me also reconsider: is skipping the final save on firstErr INTENTIONAL? The context pack unknown #8 flags it as undocumented. For persist errors, skipping final save makes sense (it would likely fail again). But for context.Canceled — the whole POINT of graceful cancel is to persist terminal states. The debounced persist might have failed due to ctx; the final forced save (`save()` = persist force=true) bypasses BOTH the version skip and the debounce wait (force skips timer). Force path: no ctx select! So save() WOULD succeed even with cancelled ctx. The code deliberately made force bypass ctx — evidence that the author intended final saves to run during cancellation — but the loadFirstErr early-return preempts reaching save(). That's a strong signal of a real bug: the force-save design intent is defeated by the early return when firstErr == context.Canceled.

Wait — one more check: is firstErr actually set on plain SIGINT with no other errors? Sequence for a clean mid-flight SIGINT:
- Scheduler loop condition `ctx.Err() == nil` → exits promptly (if active==0). If active>0, workers still running; their StartRun returns cancelled results.
- Worker: applyExecutionResult(update,...) — update succeeds unless persist hits debounce window with ctx done. If it succeeds: NO error recorded from that call. recordHistory: appendRunHistoryWithKeys — file I/O, no ctx → succeeds. publicationJobs <- res (completed only).
- Publisher goroutine: s.publishExecution(ctx, ...) → gitpublish Publish with cancelled ctx → likely returns error → recordErr → firstErr = context.Canceled (or git-specific wrapped error).

Hmm — so with a publisher configured and ≥1 completed task during the cancel window, firstErr gets set almost surely. Without publisher, firstErr set only if a persist hits the debounce race. So: **Ctrl-C during an active run with publications pending → early return → final save skipped → in-memory terminal states (cancelled statuses applied by drained workers) lost from run-state.json** (unless a debounced persist raced successfully). Next resume: reconcile converts Running→Pending (they were marked running in last successful persist), history restore may resurrect completions. Data not corrupted but the "records cancelled tasks + saves" AC is violated nondeterministically.

Let me verify what tests exist for cancellation. Read run_loop_test.go fully.

Also **Candidate E: `markTaskCancelled` for claimed-but-unstarted tasks records history with Attempts unchanged** — dedupe key uses CompletedAt nano — unique. OK.

**Candidate F: emitTask Started at claim; if worker's dependency gate puts it Waiting (synthesis deps incomplete — can't happen from scheduler selection)... skip.

**Candidate G: runLoopScope synthesis exclusion**: sourceFiltered && len(applicable)==len(allApplicable) → include synthesis. If filter selects ALL sources explicitly, synthesis included. Good.

**Candidate H: `filterRunState(state, scope)` for result.ScopeCounts — scope empty → Complete=true, Tasks=nil → runLoopStatus(…)=Completed. Filtered run with zero applicable pairs reports "completed". Edge.

**Candidate I: DB-authoritative + reconcileInterruptedRunLocked → SaveRunState writes DB; marker removal; consistent. LoadRunState prefers DB. OK. But `reconcileInterruptedRunLocked` uses LoadRunState directly (DB-aware) — good.

**Candidate J: `archiveRunStateIfExists` collision (pack #3): two resets within same second → second rename REPLACES first archive (os.Rename overwrites on unix). Reset twice quickly → earlier archive silently lost. Requires --reset twice in <1s with confirmation prompt between (interactive "y") — plausible scripted with --yes. Low severity, real.

**Candidate K: `readMemoryPressure` called EVERY scheduler iteration — /proc parse per iteration; iterations happen per worker completion + 30s disk-pause sleeps. Cheap enough. Diagnostics samples read ~10 /proc files per child per 5s tick — bounded by parallelism. OK.

**Candidate L: diagnostics.sample called inside persist() while holding saveMu → serializes state saves behind /proc reads + JSON encode + file append. Under memory pressure sampling cost grows. Minor.

**Candidate M: `SummarizeRunStateCounts(state, ...)` in progressFor reads shared `state` — called under mu via emit paths. emitRetryWait calls req.Progress directly WITHOUT mu (line 444-448): `emitRetryWait(state, scope, result.StatePath, req.Progress)` — wait, it's called with mu held! Look:

```go
waitUntilRetry(ctx, *nextRetry, func() {
    mu.Lock()
    defer mu.Unlock()
    emitRetryWait(state, scope, result.StatePath, req.Progress)
})
```

mu held while emitting. OK safe. But waitUntilRetry is only reached when active==0, so no concurrent mutators anyway.

**Candidate N: `progressFor` closure captures `state` — the RunState value (struct with slice header). SummarizeRunStateCounts iterates state.Tasks — under mu. Fine.

**Candidate O: `result.Publications` appended from publisher goroutine WITHOUT mu (line 257)!** `result.Publications = append(result.Publications, published.Publications...)` — publisher goroutine is the ONLY writer to result.Publications (main goroutine appends at line 468 AFTER `<-publicationDone`, properly ordered). Single consumer goroutine + post-drain main appends: happens-before established by channel close/receive. Safe.

**Candidate P: `publicationJobs <- res` — buffered len(state.Tasks); can't block indefinitely since capacity ≥ total tasks and only completed results enqueued ≤1 per task per invocation... EXCEPT retries: a task could complete multiple times? Once completed it's terminal; attempted blocks. Only 1 completion per task per invocation. Capacity fine.

**Candidate Q: In runTask, `dependencyState := cloneRunState(state)` — FULL state clone per task START (in addition to recordHistory clone per END). O(N) per task ×2. Plus persist clones full state per transition (~every task has ≥2 transitions: claim + terminal, plus session checkpoints!). checkpointSession → update → persist(force=false) → clone full state EACH session event. Sessions checkpoint on session events — could be many times per task. Each clone deep-copies ALL tasks incl. AgentMetadata slices. For a 200-task study with avg 2KB task states = 400KB per clone; hundreds of clones = manageable GC churn honestly. But combined with appendRunHistoryWithKeys reading+rewriting the ENTIRE history file per terminal record (O(N²) bytes), large studies get quadratic I/O. Is there a scale where this bites concretely? 1000 tasks × 2KB record = 2MB file; rewriting 2MB×1000 = 2GB written + 1000 fsyncs. Hours of overhead? fsync ~5ms → 5s total; 2GB write at 100MB/s → 20s. Meh — noticeable but not fatal. It IS a performance hazard worth noting under my lens (tests never exercise scale). Confidence medium, severity low-medium.

Now, the **ResumeValidate + Restore interplay defect candidate**:

Scenario: crash mid-run. State on disk: some tasks running (stale). Next invocation: Reconcile preserves prior states; ResumeValidate: running→pending; RestoreCompletedRunHistory restores pending tasks with valid artifacts+history to completed. Good.

BUT notice RestoreCompletedRunHistory restores ANALYSIS tasks and SYNTHESIS tasks — for synthesis it requires dependenciesComplete against current state. Restored analyses make synth deps complete → synth restored if artifact valid. Ordering handled (analysis pass first).

Subtle hole: restore requires `record.ValidationStatus == ValidationStatusPassed` — records carry validation status from terminal transitions. Validation summary set on completed results (applyExecutionResult sets Validation only if res.Validation.Path != ""). RunAnalysis with DeferPublication=true returns result WITH Validation populated. OK.

Another subtle thing in ResumeValidate: completed task whose validation NOW fails → Status=Failed, LastError set, but **CompletedAt remains set** (stale). Then scheduler reruns it (failed runnable). Claim clears CompletedAt. History key for the new terminal will differ. But if instead the study completes scheduling with this Failed task (no rerun because... no, failed IS runnable and will rerun). Unless stopScheduling. Fine.

**Now the BIGGEST remaining candidate areas: locks tests + CancelRunLoop PID-reuse + the `--continue` flag dead + CLI error mapping + web startup reconcile wedge.** Let me read the tests now — that's central to my verification lens.

Key test observations:

1. **TestRunLoopCancellationDoesNotCancelUnscheduledTasks** — cancels ctx BEFORE RunLoop, so no worker ever starts; the loop exits immediately with active==0. It verifies unscheduled tasks stay pending and no history. **It never tests cancellation DURING active work** — i.e., the drain path where workers return cancelled results and persist must record them. The exact path where I hypothesized firstErr=context.Canceled → early return → skipped final save is untested. This is a verification gap: AC:50 "cancellation ... waits, saves, records cancelled/retryable tasks" has NO test exercising mid-flight cancellation.

Let me verify my claim by tracing once more what happens on mid-flight cancel in the current code:

- Worker running StartRun(ctx...) — fake runtime ignores ctx mostly; real runtime returns cancelled result.
- runTask: res.Status = ExecutionStatusCancelled (via statusForRuntimeFailure) or err!=nil → res = RuntimeFailed.
- applyExecutionResult(update,...) → update applies mutation, then persist(id,false).
  - persist: saveMu; !force; if within 250ms of lastPersisted → select ctx.Done() → RETURN context.Canceled WITHOUT SAVING.
  - Else proceeds: clone + SaveRunState → succeeds (no ctx use in file write).
- recordErr(applyExecutionResult(...)) → possibly firstErr = context.Canceled.

Hmm wait — actually even when persist succeeds, are there other recordErr(ctx-cancelled-error) sources? 
  - `recordHistory` — no ctx → fine.
  - publisher goroutine publishExecution(ctx,...) → gitpublish Publish(ctx) — need to check whether it returns ctx.Err() when ctx done. Very likely yes (git commands with exec.CommandContext). So with s.publisher != nil and ≥1 completed publication queued during cancel → firstErr set.
  
Also markTaskCancelled for claimed-but-unstarted tasks: update→persist may hit the debounce window → error recorded → firstErr set.

So mid-flight SIGINT:
- If ANY of those records firstErr → early return before final forced save/SyncRunHistory/publish.
- Result: terminal states that were applied in memory but whose debounced persist got cancelled are LOST on disk (state file still shows running/older). History ledger: recordHistory succeeded (appended), so ledger says cancelled/completed but state file disagrees. On resume: reconcile converts stale running→pending; RestoreCompletedRunHistory re-completes those with valid artifacts+history. So system self-heals EXCEPT for cancelled tasks: history has cancelled records but restore only restores completed ones → task returns to Pending and RERUNS after user explicitly Ctrl-C'd it. Hmm — is that bad? After Ctrl-C, user expects resume to continue remaining work anyway. Cancelled evidence lost though ("records cancelled/retryable tasks" AC violated).

But WAIT — there's an even more direct question: does the epilogue's final save get skipped in the COMMON SIGINT case even without any persist failure? The common case: ctx cancelled while 2 workers active; both finish with cancelled results; their persists happen >250ms apart typically (tasks take seconds-minutes) so debounce window rarely hits... Actually lastPersisted updates on every successful persist; multiple workers finishing simultaneously DO hit the window (persist #1 succeeds, persist #2 within 250ms waits → ctx fires → fails). With parallelism ≥2, likely at least one persist fails during drain → firstErr set → skip final save.

And crucially: **the publisher goroutine will almost always set firstErr on cancellation** since publishExecution uses ctx. Let me confirm gitpublish.Publish honors ctx. Check internal/platform/gitpublish.

Also check CLI mapping: mapStudyRunLoopError(context.Canceled)? Let me read study_commands.go relevant sections.

2. **No test for waitUntilRetry/retry scheduling?** No test covers retrying taxonomy in run_loop_test.go! executionShouldRetry/defaultRuntimeRetryDelay/retryAfterFromAgent untested here — maybe in runtime_metadata_test.go. Let me check.

3. Tests use fakes writing files directly — reasonable offline approach per AC:60. Fine.

No test exercises: disk pressure pause loop, memory throttle (maybe diagnostics tests), lock steal during run, DB-authoritative mode for run-loop (state_database has no test file? state_test.go maybe), Reset archive collision, reconcileInterruptedRun marker+history-sync-failure wedge, CancelRunLoop cross-process signaling (locks_test may).

228: 	for {
229: 		select {
230: 		case <-ctx.Done():
231: 			return
232: 		case <-owned.stop:
233: 			return
234: 		case now := <-ticker.C:
235: 			snapshot, err := m.repository.Snapshot(ctx, owned.fence.RunID)
236: 			if err != nil {
237: 				owned.cancel()
238: 				return
239: 			}
240: 			if snapshot.Cancellation.State == runcontrol.CancellationRequested {
241: 				if _, _, err := m.repository.AcknowledgeCancellation(ctx, owned.fence); err != nil {
242: 					owned.cancel()
243: 					return
244: 				}
245: 				owned.cancel()
246: 				return
247: 			}
248: 			if now.Sub(lastHeartbeat) >= runcontrol.HeartbeatInterval {
249: 				if _, err := m.repository.Heartbeat(ctx, owned.fence, runcontrol.OwnerLeaseDuration); err != nil {
250: 					owned.cancel()
251: 					return
252: 				}
253: 				lastHeartbeat = now
254: 			}
255: 			if now.Sub(lastReconcile) >= runcontrol.ReconciliationInterval {
256: 				if _, err := m.repository.Reconcile(ctx, runcontrol.NativeProcessProbe{}, runcontrol.ReconcileOptions{}); err != nil {
257: 					owned.cancel()
258: 					return
259: 				}
260: 				lastReconcile = now
261: 			}
262: 		}
263: 	}
264: }

267: 	m.mu.Lock()
268: 	owned := m.owned[runID]
269: 	delete(m.owned, runID)
270: 	m.mu.Unlock()
271: 	if owned == nil {
272: 		return nil
273: 	}
274: 	owned.eventMu.Lock()
275: 	if owned.omitted > 0 {
276: 		_, _, appendErr := appendRunEventWithRetry(ctx, m.repository, owned.fence, runcontrol.EventDraft{Type: runcontrol.EventOmission, Omission: &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: "equivalent progress coalesced", Count: owned.omitted, FirstAt: &owned.omittedFirst, LastAt: &owned.omittedLast}})
277: 		if appendErr != nil && runErr == nil {
278: 			runErr = appendErr
279: 		}
280: 		owned.omitted = 0
281: 	}
282: 	owned.eventMu.Unlock()
283: 	close(owned.stop)
284: 	<-owned.done
285: 	owned.cancel()
286: 	outcome := runcontrol.TerminalSucceeded
287: 	reason := "operation completed"
288: 	switch {
289: 	case errors.Is(runErr, context.DeadlineExceeded):
290: 		outcome, reason = runcontrol.TerminalTimedOut, "operation deadline exceeded"
291: 	case errors.Is(runErr, context.Canceled), state == OperationCancelled:
292: 		outcome, reason = runcontrol.TerminalCancelled, "operation cancelled"
293: 	case runErr != nil, state == OperationFailed:

295: 	case state == OperationPartial:

297: 	}

93: func newDurableOperationManager(repository runcontrol.Repository, owner runcontrol.Owner) *durableOperationManager {
94: 	return &durableOperationManager{repository: repository, owner: owner, owned: make(map[string]*ownedDurableOperation)}

97: func (m *durableOperationManager) AcceptOperation(ctx context.Context, confirmation Confirmation, digest string) (AcceptedOperation, error) {
98: 	req := confirmation.Request
99: 	target := runcontrol.Target{
100: 		Kind: "operation", Operation: string(req.Kind), Project: req.Project, Sprint: req.Sprint,
101: 		Study: req.Study, Stage: req.Stage, Task: req.Task,
102: 	}
103: 	snapshot, err := m.repository.Accept(ctx, runcontrol.Acceptance{
104: 		Target: target, ProductStatus: "prepared", OperationAlias: digest, ConfirmationDigest: digest,
105: 	})
106: 	if err != nil && digest != "" && errors.Is(err, runcontrol.ErrConflict) {
107: 		existing, resolveErr := m.repository.ResolveOperationAlias(ctx, digest)
108: 		if resolveErr != nil {
109: 			return AcceptedOperation{}, errors.Join(err, resolveErr)
110: 		}
111: 		return AcceptedOperation{RunID: string(existing.RunID), Context: ctx, Existing: true, Lifecycle: string(existing.Lifecycle)}, nil
112: 	}
113: 	if err != nil {
114: 		return AcceptedOperation{}, fmt.Errorf("persist confirmed operation acceptance: %w", err)
115: 	}
116: 	attempt, _, err := m.repository.Claim(ctx, runcontrol.Claim{RunID: snapshot.RunID, Owner: m.owner, Lease: runcontrol.OwnerLeaseDuration})
117: 	if err != nil {
118: 		return AcceptedOperation{}, fmt.Errorf("persist confirmed operation owner claim: %w", err)
119: 	}
120: 	fence := runcontrol.Fence{RunID: snapshot.RunID, AttemptID: attempt.ID, OwnerID: m.owner.ID, FencingGeneration: attempt.FencingGeneration}
121: 	if _, _, err := appendRunEventWithRetry(ctx, m.repository, fence, runcontrol.EventDraft{
122: 		Type: runcontrol.EventLifecycle, Lifecycle: runcontrol.LifecycleRunning,
123: 		Payload: map[string]string{"lifecycle": string(runcontrol.LifecycleRunning)},
124: 	}); err != nil {
125: 		terminalCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
126: 		_, _, _ = proposeRunTerminalWithRetry(terminalCtx, m.repository, fence, runcontrol.TerminalProposal{Outcome: runcontrol.TerminalPersistenceLost, Reason: "operation start persistence failed", ProposedBy: m.owner.ID})
127: 		cancel()
128: 		return AcceptedOperation{}, fmt.Errorf("persist confirmed operation start: %w", err)
129: 	}
130: 	operationCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(runcontrol.WithParentRun(ctx, snapshot.RunID))
131: 	operationCtx = context.WithValue(operationCtx, durableOperationContextKey{}, durableOperationOwnership{repository: m.repository, fence: fence})
132: 	owned := &ownedDurableOperation{fence: fence, cancel: cancel, stop: make(chan struct{}), done: make(chan struct{})}
133: 	m.mu.Lock()
134: 	m.owned[string(snapshot.RunID)] = owned
135: 	m.mu.Unlock()
136: 	go m.controlOperation(operationCtx, owned)
137: 	return AcceptedOperation{RunID: string(snapshot.RunID), Context: operationCtx, Lifecycle: string(runcontrol.LifecycleRunning)}, nil
138: }

140: func qaOwnershipFromContext(ctx context.Context) (sprint.QAWriterToken, func(sprint.QAWriterToken) error, error) {
141: 	ownership, ok := ctx.Value(durableOperationContextKey{}).(durableOperationOwnership)
142: 	if !ok || ownership.repository == nil {
143: 		return sprint.QAWriterToken{}, nil, errors.New("durable QA ownership is missing from the operation context")
144: 	}
145: 	token := sprint.QAWriterToken{RunID: string(ownership.fence.RunID), OperationalAttemptID: string(ownership.fence.AttemptID), FencingGeneration: ownership.fence.FencingGeneration}
146: 	fence := func(got sprint.QAWriterToken) error {
147: 		if got != token {
148: 			return runcontrol.ErrStaleFence
149: 		}
150: 		fenceCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 30*time.Second)
151: 		defer cancel()
152: 		_, err := ownership.repository.Heartbeat(fenceCtx, ownership.fence, runControlLease)
153: 		return err
154: 	}
155: 	return token, fence, nil
156: }

158: func (m *durableOperationManager) RecordOperationEvent(ctx context.Context, runID string, event OperationEvent) (bool, error) {
159: 	m.mu.Lock()
160: 	owned := m.owned[runID]
161: 	m.mu.Unlock()
162: 	if owned == nil {
163: 		return false, runcontrol.ErrNotFound
164: 	}
165: 	owned.eventMu.Lock()
166: 	defer owned.eventMu.Unlock()
167: 	eventType := runcontrol.EventProgress
168: 	if event.State == OperationFailed {
169: 		eventType = runcontrol.EventWarning
170: 	}
171: 	key := string(eventType) + "\x00" + event.Stage + "\x00" + event.Task + "\x00" + event.PhaseState + "\x00" + event.SafeSummary + "\x00" + event.EventType + "\x00" + event.EventKind + "\x00" + event.Tool + "\x00" + event.Reason + "\x00" + event.Detail
172: 	now := time.Now().UTC()
173: 	elapsed := now.Sub(owned.progressAt)
174: 	if eventType == runcontrol.EventProgress && key == owned.progressKey && elapsed >= 0 && elapsed < runcontrol.ProgressCoalesceWindow {
175: 		if owned.omitted == 0 {
176: 			owned.omittedFirst = now
177: 		}
178: 		owned.omitted++
179: 		owned.omittedLast = now
180: 		return false, nil
181: 	}
182: 	payload := map[string]string{
183: 		"state": string(event.State), "type": event.EventType,
184: 		"count": fmt.Sprintf("%d/%d", event.Completed, event.Total),
185: 	}
186: 	for key, value := range map[string]string{
187: 		"phase_state": event.PhaseState, "summary": event.SafeSummary,
188: 		"tool_call_id": event.ToolCallID, "tool_status": event.ToolStatus,
189: 		"tool_arguments": event.ToolArguments, "tool_result": event.ToolResult, "tool_error": event.ToolError,
190: 		"provider": event.Provider, "model": event.Model, "harness": event.Harness,
191: 	} {
192: 		if value != "" {
193: 			payload[key] = value
194: 		}
195: 	}
196: 	var omission *runcontrol.Omission
197: 	if event.Message != "" {
198: 		omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: "presentation message omitted", Count: 1}
199: 	}
200: 	if owned.omitted > 0 {
201: 		if omission == nil {
202: 			omission = &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: "equivalent progress coalesced"}
203: 		}
204: 		omission.Count += owned.omitted
205: 		omission.FirstAt, omission.LastAt = &owned.omittedFirst, &owned.omittedLast
206: 		owned.omitted = 0
207: 	}
208: 	_, _, err := appendRunEventWithRetry(ctx, m.repository, owned.fence, runcontrol.EventDraft{
209: 		Type: eventType, Scope: runcontrol.EventScopeOperation, Stage: event.Stage, Task: event.Task,
210: 		Kind: event.EventKind, Tool: event.Tool, Action: event.Action, Reason: event.Reason,
211: 		Detail: event.Detail, Payload: payload, Omission: omission,
212: 	})
213: 	if err != nil {
214: 		owned.cancel()
215: 		return false, err
216: 	}
217: 	if eventType == runcontrol.EventProgress {
218: 		owned.progressKey, owned.progressAt = key, now
219: 	}
220: 	return true, nil
221: }

223: func (m *durableOperationManager) controlOperation(ctx context.Context, owned *ownedDurableOperation) {
224: 	defer close(owned.done)
225: 	ticker := time.NewTicker(runcontrol.OwnerTickInterval)
226: 	defer ticker.Stop()
227: 	lastHeartbeat, lastReconcile := time.Now(), time.Now()
228: 	for {
229: 		select {
230: 		case <-ctx.Done():
231: 			return
232: 		case <-owned.stop:
233: 			return
234: 		case now := <-ticker.C:
235: 			snapshot, err := m.repository.Snapshot(ctx, owned.fence.RunID)
236: 			if err != nil {
237: 				owned.cancel()
238: 				return
239: 			}
240: 			if snapshot.Cancellation.State == runcontrol.CancellationRequested {
241: 				if _, _, err := m.repository.AcknowledgeCancellation(ctx, owned.fence); err != nil {
242: 					owned.cancel()
243: 					return
244: 				}
245: 				owned.cancel()
246: 				return
247: 			}
248: 			if now.Sub(lastHeartbeat) >= runcontrol.HeartbeatInterval {
249: 				if _, err := m.repository.Heartbeat(ctx, owned.fence, runcontrol.OwnerLeaseDuration); err != nil {
250: 					owned.cancel()
251: 					return
252: 				}
253: 				lastHeartbeat = now
254: 			}
255: 			if now.Sub(lastReconcile) >= runcontrol.ReconciliationInterval {
256: 				if _, err := m.repository.Reconcile(ctx, runcontrol.NativeProcessProbe{}, runcontrol.ReconcileOptions{}); err != nil {
257: 					owned.cancel()
258: 					return
259: 				}
260: 				lastReconcile = now
261: 			}
262: 		}
263: 	}
264: }

266: func (m *durableOperationManager) FinishOperation(ctx context.Context, runID string, state OperationState, runErr error) error {
267: 	m.mu.Lock()
268: 	owned := m.owned[runID]
269: 	delete(m.owned, runID)
270: 	m.mu.Unlock()
271: 	if owned == nil {
272: 		return nil
273: 	}
274: 	owned.eventMu.Lock()
275: 	if owned.omitted > 0 {
276: 		_, _, appendErr := appendRunEventWithRetry(ctx, m.repository, owned.fence, runcontrol.EventDraft{Type: runcontrol.EventOmission, Omission: &runcontrol.Omission{Reason: "equivalent progress coalesced", Count: owned.omitted, FirstAt: &owned.omittedFirst, LastAt: &owned.omittedLast}})
277: 		if appendErr != nil && runErr == nil {
278: 			runErr = appendErr
279: 		}
280: 		owned.omitted = 0
281: 	}
282: 	owned.eventMu.Unlock()
283: 	close(owned.stop)
284: 	<-owned.done
285: 	owned.cancel()
286: 	outcome := runcontrol.TerminalSucceeded
287: 	reason := "operation completed"
288: 	switch {
289: 	case errors.Is(runErr, context.DeadlineExceeded):
290: 		outcome, reason = runcontrol.TerminalTimedOut, "operation deadline exceeded"
291: 	case errors.Is(runErr, context.Canceled), state == OperationCancelled:
292: 		outcome, reason = runcontrol.TerminalCancelled, "operation cancelled"
293: 	case runErr != nil, state == OperationFailed:
294: 		outcome, reason = runcontrol.TerminalFailed, "operation failed"
295: 	case state == OperationPartial:
296: 		outcome, reason = runcontrol.TerminalInterrupted, "operation interrupted"
297: 	}
298: 	_, _, err := proposeRunTerminalWithRetry(ctx, m.repository, owned.fence, runcontrol.TerminalProposal{Outcome: outcome, Reason: reason, ProposedBy: m.owner.ID})
299: 	return err
300: }

	// Model optionally overrides the runtime model (provider/model) for this

	Model               string

}

type SynthesisRequest struct {
	StudyRef     string
	DimensionRef string
	SourceRefs   []string
	// Model optionally overrides the runtime model (provider/model) for this

	Model               string
	OnEvent             func(runtimepkg.Event)

	DeferPublication    bool
}

	StudyRef      string
	DimensionRefs []string

	// Model optionally overrides the runtime model (provider/model) for every

	TaskKind     TaskKind

---
The browser's operation handle, event replay, confirmation, and subscriber are
bounded, ephemeral views. Product-owned workspace/run state is authoritative.

- Refresh, navigation, tab close, SSE loss, and a slow subscriber cancel only
  observation. They do not prove completion and do not cancel product work.
- On `recovery_required`, reconnect exhaustion, operation expiry, or a missing
  terminal event, follow the durable refresh link or run the equivalent CLI
  status/validation command before retrying.
- Explicit cancellation is idempotent. A late cancel cannot replace an already
  authoritative completion/failure result.
- During shutdown, new mutations receive `server_draining`; wait for the server
  to stop, inspect durable status, then restart and retry preparation.
- A `.cleanup-uncertain.json` marker means bounded shutdown could not prove
  cleanup. Restart reconciliation runs through the owning sprint/study module;
  process absence and artifact presence are evidence only, not success.
- A stale product mutation lock must be assessed through normal CLI status and
  lock guidance. Never delete it merely because the browser operation expired.

## Locks And `--force-unlock`

`run-loop` uses a per-study lock to refuse concurrent runs. Use:

```bash
ultraplan study <study> status
```

to inspect lock path, PID, command, and acquisition time.

Use `--force-unlock` only when an operator has confirmed the existing lock is stale:

```bash
ultraplan study <study> run-loop --force-unlock
```

Forcing an active lock can corrupt operator expectations, duplicate runtime work, and race report writes.

part.text: The scheduler is stuck in the disk-pressure admission loop (`run_loop.go:394`) with a live `/tmp` disk reading. Checking whether the test stubs disk pressure and what the host filesystem looks like.

reasoning_details.text:
Very interesting! The hang:

- Main test goroutine stuck in `RunLoop` at run_loop.go:394 — that's the disk-pressure admission pause `select { <-ctx.Done() / <-timer.C }` with a 30s timer, looping forever. So the scheduler is in the **disk-pressure admission-paused infinite loop** (active==0 → 30s sleep → re-check → still pressured...). With ctx = Background (never cancelled), this loop NEVER exits while disk stays pressured.
- Meanwhile goroutine 9 is blocked reading `/proc/self/status` via processMemory inside diagnostics sample.

Why is disk pressured in the test? readSchedulerDiskPressure is REAL here (test doesn't stub it?) — let me look at run_history_test.go:107 context. The test runs RunLoop with real disk reader; if the machine's filesystem holding /tmp has <1.5GiB available OR ≥90% used, Pressured=true forever → infinite admission pause. On THIS machine, /tmp or the workspace fs must be low/space-tight.

Wait but goroutine 9 blocked on a READ syscall of /proc/self/status for a long time? That's odd — reading /proc/self/status shouldn't block. Unless... procfs read blocking happens under heavy VM pressure. OR the scanner hit a partial state? Whatever — secondary.

KEY QUESTION: is this a product defect or environment artifact? The admission-pause loop at :384-400: when active==0 and ctx never cancelled and disk stays pressured → loop every 30s forever. It DOES call CleanupRuntimeStores each iteration with aggressive=true (active==0) to free space. If cleanup can't free enough (disk full from EXTERNAL causes), RunLoop hangs FOREVER with no cancellation escape except ctx cancel — CLI Ctrl-C works (ctx cancels). So operationally it's "pause until space frees" by design.

But there's a REAL defect flavor here: **the loop never terminates when nothing can change** — e.g., study outputs themselves fill the disk, or the threshold can't be reached because total disk is small (1.5GiB minimum free required; a small volume < 1.5GiB total can NEVER satisfy `AvailableBytes <= 1.5GiB ⇒ cap 0`... wait cap 0 means paused; recovery requires avail > 1.5GiB — impossible on a 1GiB volume!). On any filesystem smaller than 1.5GiB free-able, run-loop admission pauses forever (until user aborts). More realistically: a volume that hovers at ≥90% used triggers Pressured regardless of absolute bytes (`percent >= 90`); if the workspace lives on a perpetually-90%-full volume, same infinite pause.

Hmm, but is that a DEFECT vs intended backpressure? Intended: wait for space. The design flaw: no exit/reporting path when the condition cannot resolve; combined with tests not stubbing disk pressure here → the SUITE HANGS on constrained machines rather than failing. That's exactly my lens: verification suite produces a hang (not a failure) depending on host disk state — CI machines with small/temp-fs disks will hang the whole package. And notably the OTHER tests stub readSchedulerDiskPressure but this one doesn't.

Let me confirm: does TestRunLoopWritesRunHistoryAndSummary stub disk? Read run_history_test.go around line 60-130.

Also check machine's /tmp free space to explain Pressured. t.TempDir uses TMPDIR usually /tmp. statfs -f /tmp.

Also: WHY didn't the baseline (pack) catch this? Pack claims green baseline at 8eef70f. Maybe at that commit the test didn't exist or didn't hit the loop; or the pack's baseline ran on a machine with ample disk. The hang is environment-sensitive: requires avail<1.5GiB or used≥90% on the test tmp fs. Our sandbox likely has a small overlay fs. Let me check df.

reasoning_details.text:
CONFIRMED: `TestRunLoopWritesRunHistoryAndSummary` does NOT stub `readSchedulerDiskPressure`, unlike `TestRunLoopRefills...` which stubs it to a healthy value. The host `/tmp` is tmpfs with **1.5G available** — and the admission threshold is `available <= 1.5GiB ⇒ Pressured`. 1.5G avail ≈ 1.5GiB (1610612736 bytes avail vs threshold 1536MiB=1608599552 bytes). df says Avail 1.5G; precise bytes matter: if avail ≤ 1536MiB, Pressured=true → infinite pause loop (30s sleeps) with Background ctx → test hangs forever.

So on any dev/CI machine whose temp filesystem has ≤1.5GiB free (very common for container tmpfs), `go test ./internal/study` HANGS INDEFINITELY rather than failing. That's a concrete verification-suite defect: the test suite's outcome depends on host disk state, producing a hang (worse than failure — eats the whole CI timeout, no diagnosis). Also proves the production behavior: run-loop on a volume with ≤1.5GiB free that cleanup can't fix spins forever printing "disk pressure paused new workers" every 30s with no exit criterion. Design intent = wait for space; acceptable operationally IF ctx-cancellable (it is) — but the unbounded wait with only 30s sleeps and no escalation/reporting path when nothing changes is worth flagging as part of the test-hang finding, not separately.

Wait, actually let me double check the numbers: minimumRuntimeFreeBytes = 1536*1024*1024 = 1,608,599,552 ≈ 1.498 GiB. /tmp avail "1.5G". If actual avail bytes > threshold at some moments, loop would exit. The stack shows it stuck in the pause select — so at loop time avail ≤ threshold. tmpfs fills as tests write; earlier tests consumed space. Also note: the diagnostics goroutine blocked reading /proc/self/status — under tmpfs pressure? weird but secondary; actually it might just have been mid-read at dump time... a read syscall parked in poll ignoringEINTRIO — /proc reads can block on kernel locks under memory pressure. Whatever.

Also NOTE: this hang did NOT reproduce in the pack's baseline claim ("go test ./..., -race green") because that ran on a machine/filesystem state with more space (or before tmpfs filled). Environment-dependent hang = misleading verification.

Is this within my surface? Yes: run_loop.go disk-pressure logic + missing stub in a run-loop test. Two-part finding:
(F2a) Test suite hangs on hosts with ≤~1.5GiB free tmp: TestRunLoopWritesRunHistoryAndSummary lacks the disk-pressure stub its siblings use; scheduler's admission-pause loop never terminates under Background ctx.
(F2b) Production corollary: admission-pause loop has no give-up/diagnose path when space cannot be freed (e.g., small volumes where 1.5GiB floor exceeds capacity); operator sees infinite 30s-cycle pause. Lower severity since Ctrl-C works.

Let me verify F2b reachability nuance: CleanupRuntimeStores aggressive=true runs each cycle; if study dir is tiny, frees nothing; loop continues forever. Yes.

Also confirm the OTHER run-loop tests stub disk but this one doesn't — grep readSchedulerDiskPressure in tests.
